why: Both runs cover all 52 passages (P01-P52) exactly once, so coverage does not separate them; the disagreement is only how finely three sections are split, plus where the two closing passages go. In 2.3 run A separates spermatogenesis and its hormonal control (P23-P25) from sperm structure and semen (P26-P28); in 2.5 it separates fertilisation (P38-P40) from cleavage, blastocyst and implantation (P42-P43); in 2.6 it separates the placenta and pregnancy hormones (P44-P46) from the month-by-month embryonic development (P47-P48). Each of those three pairs is a place where a single question can target one half and not the other, so the split is the unit a question links to and run B's merges would put two distinct question families under one name. Run B's remaining difference, a subtopic named 'Chapter summary and exercises' for P51-P52, names a location rather than an idea; run A's placement of those two chapter-level passages with the chapter-overview subtopic keeps every subtopic an idea while still covering them. Nothing in run B is right where run A is wrong, so A is correct as-is and no merge is needed.
note: The adjudication input's evidence block contains only chapter, chapter_title and headings (2.1-2.7); it does not include the passage list with ids, kinds and first 200 characters that the step's agents saw. This decision therefore rests on the section structure, the contiguous passage-id ranges, and the two runs' own groupings and names, not on passage text. The one difference where passage text would have mattered is the placement of P51-P52: both runs treat them as chapter-closing material, and they are covered either way, so the choice between them does not affect coverage. from_heading values for the chapter-level subtopic ('Chapter 2 introduction' in A, '2' in B) are not among the seven headings supplied in the evidence.
